name: Driving Creek Artist in Residence Programme

eligibility.eligibility_notes: Official page: 'Driving Creek residency panel selects artists for residencies 4 times per year' and the call is open to 'any form of artist'. No nationality, residency or career-stage restriction is stated anywhere on the page, but international eligibility is not spelled out in so many words. Confirm with the pottery before applying. Up to 5 artists per quarter.

funding.stipend_detail: None. Official wording: 'there is no fee for the artist residency' and 'we offer free artist residencies'. Nothing is paid to the artist.
funding.materials_budget: None stated. Artists are asked to 'chip in here and there to keep the co-operative spirit of the pottery alive'.
funding.application_fee: None stated; official wording 'there is no fee for the artist residency'

discipline.programme_focus: Working pottery and railway founded by Barry Brickell, with shared studio spaces, wood-fired and gas kilns, native forest setting. Residents have worked across ceramics, painting, sculpture, photography and textiles.

deadline_notes: Quarterly cycles. Official wording: 'April - June, applications close at the end of September'; 'July - September, applications close at the end of December'; 'October - December, applications close at the end of March'; 'January - March, applications close at the end of June'. The 30 September 2026 date is for the April to June 2027 quarter; the next is 31 December 2026 for July to September 2027. Exact day not stated on the page, 'end of' month is the official wording.
duration: Up to one 3-month quarter (Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep, Oct-Dec)
money_summary: No fee, no stipend. Free basic on-site accommodation, shared studio and kilns. Artist pays travel, food and materials.
style_fit_reason: A ceramics-led co-operative with real kilns and a sculpture-friendly, hands-on culture. Good for material work; no particular leaning toward surreal or figurative practice, and no fabrication support beyond the pottery.
cautions: Unfunded: no stipend, travel or materials. Only accommodation and studio are free.
International eligibility is implied by the absence of restrictions, not stated. Confirm by email before applying.
Accommodation is described as 'basic' and shared; up to five residents at once.
Visa: nothing on the page. An Indian passport holder needs a New Zealand visitor visa; check whether a 3-month unpaid residency is permitted under it.
notes: Confirmed from the official residency page on 2026-09-23. Deadline for the April to June 2027 quarter is the end of September 2026, so this is open for one more week; the December deadline is the realistic target. Application is via JotForm.

name: BigCi (Bilpin international ground for Creative initiatives) Artist Residency
location: Bilpin, Blue Mountains, New South Wales

eligibility.eligibility_notes: Official wording: 'Painters, sculptors, multimedia artists, performance artists, writers, musicians, dancers, filmmakers and other creative souls are invited to apply for the residency.' The fee page lists separate rates for 'Self-funded International artists', so international applicants are explicitly expected. No career-stage requirement.

funding.stipend_detail: Official wording: 'There is no stipend or living allowance attached to the stay.' Money flows from the artist to the residency.
funding.materials_budget: None. Art materials are the artist's cost.
funding.application_fee: Not stated. The official Artist Residency page publishes only stay rates: 'AUD$400 for International artists' per week for self-funded individuals, and 'Our rates for organisations are AUD$700 per person per week for Australian artists and AUD$800 per person per week for International artists.' There is no fee to apply mentioned, and no 'no fee' line either.

discipline.thematic_constraint: None required. The organisation notes many residents pursue environmental or ecological projects because of the Wollemi National Park setting, but says 'many others use our outstanding natural surroundings as a source of creativity for a variety of different artistic pursuits.'
discipline.programme_focus: Independent, artist-run residency on the edge of Wollemi National Park focused on artists' professional development and project facilitation. Facilities are the Art Shed, the Barn and the House on 8 acres of bushland. Residents present at a BigCi Open Day at the end of their stay.

deadline_notes: Official wording: 'Artist residency proposals are welcome throughout the year', to be submitted 'well in advance'.
duration: Flexible, an 'agreed period of time' set by the project
money_summary: Artist pays AUD 400 per week (international rate) covering accommodation, workspace, utilities and internet. No stipend. Artist also pays food, travel, insurance and materials.
style_fit_reason: Open to sculptors and multimedia artists with a shed and barn to work in, but the programme's gravity is environmental and site-based rather than figurative or surreal, and there is no fabrication support.
cautions: Fee-paying residency: roughly AUD 1,600 per four weeks before food, travel and materials.
Environmental setting shapes the programme; a dramatic figurative project would sit outside the usual resident profile.
Application fee is not stated anywhere on the official site, so it cannot be recorded as zero. Confirm before applying.
Visa: nothing on the site. Indian passport holders need an Australian visitor visa; confirm a paid residency stay is permitted.
notes: Fee schedule confirmed from the official Artist Residency page on 2026-09-23. Listed by Res Artis and TransArtists; BigCi cites collaborative links with Asialink and Artspace Sydney. UNCONFIRMED FACT, exact open question: does BigCi charge anything to submit a residency proposal, on top of the AUD 400 per week stay rate? The official page and the BigCi home page were both read on 2026-09-23 and neither states a figure nor says applying is free. Ask through the contact form on bigci.org.

name: Eramboo Artist Environment Live-in Residency
location: Terrey Hills, Sydney, New South Wales

eligibility.eligibility_notes: Official wording for the live-in residency (Studio 5): ideal for 'regional, inter-state or international artists working in all media, writers, musicians, dance or performance artists'. The separate non-residential 6-month Award with a $3,000 allowance is run with Northern Beaches Council and its 2026 round is closed; it is not the programme recorded here.

funding.stipend_detail: None for the live-in residency. Residents fund their own travel, food and art materials.
funding.application_fee: Not stated; online application form with no fee mentioned
artist_pays: residency fee AUD 250 per week (single) or AUD 300 per week (couple)

discipline.programme_focus: Bushland artist environment next to Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park offering a furnished live-in studio apartment (kitchenette, bathroom, deck, wifi, 24/7 access) for artists in all media to develop a body of work.

deadline_notes: The online application form for the live-in residency is live and lets applicants choose their own start and end dates. No closing date is stated. The 2026 non-residential AIR Award is a separate programme and is closed.
money_summary: Artist pays AUD 250 per week plus AUD 500 bond and AUD 100 cleaning fee for a furnished live-in studio. No stipend, travel or materials.
style_fit_reason: All media welcome and a private live-in studio, but it is a quiet bushland retreat with no workshop, technician or fabrication support and no stated curatorial interest in figurative or surreal work.
cautions: Fee-paying residency; the artist carries every cost.
Official page: international artists are 'responsible for arranging their own visas and travel'.
Studio apartment scale suits studio-sized work, not large installation.
Do not confuse with the funded non-residential Eramboo AIR Award, which is a Northern Beaches Council programme and closed for 2026.
notes: Fees and eligibility confirmed from the official Artist Programs page on 2026-09-23. Application form on the official site accepts international addresses.

name: Earthskin Creative Residency
location: Piha (Waygood Foundation) and Warkworth, Auckland region

eligibility.eligibility_notes: The residency page welcomes 'artists, potters, sculptors, musicians, designers, writers, and environmental innovators' with no nationality restriction stated. International eligibility is implied rather than spelled out; confirm by email.

funding.stipend_detail: None. Official wording: '$250 per week', with the cost 'reduced through work exchange' in the permaculture gardens.
funding.materials_budget: None. Official wording: 'bring your own food and art supplies'.
funding.application_fee: None stated; application is a form emailed to earthskintrust@gmail.com

discipline.thematic_constraint: Environmental stewardship. Official wording: 'The use of unnatural chemical art materials that can go into our precious land is not allowed.' Residents contribute talks, workshops, exhibitions or a gifted artwork.
discipline.programme_focus: Trust-run creative residency on a permaculture and earthbuild site at Piha and in the Warkworth valley, with studio, gallery, yurt and housing, aimed at 'deepening connection with self, community, and the land'.

deadline_notes: Official wording: 'Residencies for 2026 and 2027 open in May, please apply now.' No closing date is given; applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.
duration: 2 to 4 weeks, extendable to 1 to 3 months
money_summary: Artist pays NZD 250 per week plus utilities, food and materials, and gives one artwork as koha. No stipend.
style_fit_reason: An eco-retreat with a ban on 'unnatural chemical art materials', which rules out most resins, solvents and industrial finishes a mixed-media sculptor would use. No fabrication facilities and a land-focused ethos far from dramatic figurative work.
cautions: A koha artwork must be gifted to the trust's collection for fundraising.
No synthetic or chemical art materials permitted on site; check this against the client's actual materials before applying.
Visa not addressed on the site.
notes: Fee, koha rule and material restriction confirmed from the official residency page on 2026-09-23. Recorded so the unfunded decision has the full Oceania picture, but this is the weakest fit of the four.
